gloss: to reap; to harvest; to mow

definitions.gloss: to reap; to harvest; to mow; to cut down
definitions.explanation: To cut and gather crops, grass, or other plants. Used literally for agricultural harvesting and lawn care.

examples.japanese: {秋|あき}になると{農家|のうか}は{稲|いね}を{刈|か}り{取|と}る。
examples.english: When autumn comes, farmers harvest the rice.

examples.japanese: {雑草|ざっそう}が{伸|の}びすぎたので、{週末|しゅうまつ}にまとめて{刈|か}り{取|と}った。
examples.english: The weeds had grown too tall, so I mowed them all down over the weekend.

notes:
A compound verb from {刈|か}る (to mow, cut) + {取|と}る (to take). The {取|と}る component adds the nuance of taking or gathering what has been cut.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {稲|いね}を{刈|か}り{取|と}る: to harvest rice
- {麦|むぎ}を{刈|か}り{取|と}る: to harvest wheat
- {雑草|ざっそう}を{刈|か}り{取|と}る: to mow weeds
- {芝生|しばふ}を{刈|か}り{取|と}る: to mow the lawn

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {刈|か}る: to mow, to cut — simpler verb; focuses on the cutting action without the gathering nuance
- {収穫|しゅうかく}する: to harvest — broader term for harvesting any crop; more formal
- {摘|つ}み{取|と}る: to pick, pluck — for hand-picking fruits, flowers, or tea leaves

FIGURATIVE USE:
Occasionally used figuratively to mean reaping consequences or benefits, similar to English "you reap what you sow."
